# Resources

> Every external link the chapters recommend, grouped by chapter. All are public. Tooling moves fast; if a link is dead, search for the name.

## Part 1: Foundations

### [How LLMs work: the mechanics you steer with](../01-foundations/01-how-llms-work.md)

- [Let's build the GPT Tokenizer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zduSFxRajkE): a from-scratch walkthrough of tokenization.
- [Tiktokenizer](https://tiktokenizer.vercel.app/): paste text and see tokens, IDs and the chat-format markers.
- [What Is ChatGPT Doing ... and Why Does It Work?](https://writings.stephenwolfram.com/2023/02/what-is-chatgpt-doing-and-why-does-it-work/): an older long read on next-token prediction that is still accurate.
- [Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference](https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/defeating-nondeterminism-in-llm-inference/): why the same input can give different output even at temperature zero.
- [Why language models hallucinate](https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/): the incentives behind confident wrong answers.
- [Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.08939): evidence that the order of facts changes the result.
- [Prompt caching (Claude API docs)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching): the prefix-match mechanism, lifetimes and pricing.
- [How Claude Code uses prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching): which everyday actions keep or invalidate the cache in one harness.

### [Context engineering: what the agent sees and how to keep it useful](../01-foundations/02-context-engineering.md)

- [Explore the context window (Claude Code docs)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window): what loads when, with token counts, and what survives compaction.
- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): instruction file loading order, path-scoped rules and memory limits.
- [Best practices for Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices): the vendor's advice on telling the agent what it cannot see.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md): the open, cross-harness format for the project instruction file.
- [Context Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725): a paper arguing that models can manage their own working context, a reason to keep scaffolding light.
- [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/home): the specification for skills, the standard way to load procedures on demand.

### [Harnesses and settings](../01-foundations/03-harnesses-and-settings.md)

- [Claude Code settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings): settings files, scopes and precedence, with links to the full key reference.
- [Claude Code permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions): rule syntax, evaluation order and the limits of pattern matching.
- [Claude Code sandboxing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing): what the sandbox isolates and what it does not cover.
- [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex): OpenAI's open-source terminal agent; a second native harness to compare against.
- [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi): a minimal, multi-provider coding agent and toolkit that is easy to read and extend.
- [Herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr): a runtime that keeps terminal agents alive and lets agents manage their own sessions.

## Part 2: Your workspace

### [Instruction files and rules](../02-workspace/01-instruction-files-and-rules.md)

- [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md/): the open format for a cross-harness instruction file, with examples and the list of tools that read it.
- [Claude Code: hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): where to move an instruction that has to run at a fixed point.
- [Cursor rules](https://cursor.com/docs/rules): the same path-scoped idea in another harness.
- [Husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky/): git hooks an agent can configure once so a check always runs.

### [Skills](../02-workspace/02-skills.md)

- [Claude Code: skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills): where skills load from, the full frontmatter reference, arguments, forked context, and how to evaluate a skill.
- [skills.sh](https://skills.sh): a public directory of skills, useful for seeing many shapes.
- [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): the `npx skills` CLI for installing, listing and updating skills across harnesses.
- [How some malicious AI skills hide instructions from reviewers](https://blog.virustotal.com/2026/10/how-some-malicious-ai-skills-hide.html): why you read a skill before you install it.
- [MCP skills extension](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2640-skills-extension): the proposal that lets an MCP server publish skills next to its tools.

### [Knowledge and memory](../02-workspace/03-knowledge-and-memory.md)

- [Architectural Decision Records](https://adr.github.io/): the ADR practice, templates and tooling.
- [Open Knowledge Format](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md): Markdown with frontmatter that records a note's source, trust and freshness.
- [jevgrep](https://github.com/dzhng/jevgrep): a CLI that uses a small fast model to find relevant files for a coding agent.
- [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/): a Markdown editor that works well as the human reading view over a folder of notes.
- [Astro](https://astro.build/): a static-site generator for publishing the same Markdown or MDX files as a website.

### [Tools and MCP](../02-workspace/04-tools-and-mcp.md)

- [Model Context Protocol documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/getting-started/intro): the spec and concepts for the 2026-07-28 revision; start here before writing a server.
- [MCP SDKs](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/sdk): official client and server libraries; use one instead of hand-rolling the transport.
- [Stateless MCP proposal](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2575-stateless-mcp): why newer revisions drop the session handshake.
- [MCP Inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector): a testing tool for poking at a server by hand.
- [MCP conformance tests](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance): automated checks that a server follows the protocol.
- [Claude Code: connect to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp): adding servers, scopes, OAuth, tool search, output limits.
- [Designing an MCP gateway (Uber Engineering)](https://www.uber.com/blog/designing-mcp-gateway/): tool discovery and authorisation at thousands of tools.

### [Hooks, guardrails and security](../02-workspace/05-hooks-guardrails-and-security.md)

- [Claude Code: hooks guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide): worked examples, including protected files and the stop-hook block cap.
- [Example settings files for Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples/settings): starter configurations for stricter deployments.
- [Codex hooks](https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks): the equivalent mechanism in Codex.
- [Pi extensions](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions): how Pi lets code hook into its lifecycle.
- [Bitwarden Agent Access SDK](https://bitwarden.com/blog/introducing-agent-access-sdk/): one approach to letting agents use secrets without seeing them.
- [OpenAI moderation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/moderation?api-mode=responses): an example of a moderation model for input and output checks.

## Part 3: Building agents

### [The agent loop and its primitives](../03-agents/01-agent-loop-and-primitives.md)

- [Pi agent loop source](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts): a complete, readable loop that many other projects build on.
- [Goose](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose): another open-source harness; useful to compare how a second team solved the same problems.
- [Claude Code subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents): includes where session and subagent transcripts are stored and when they are cleaned up.
- [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents): a short, vendor-written overview of when a loop is the right tool and when a fixed workflow is better.

### [Build your own agent](../03-agents/02-build-your-own-agent.md)

- [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk): the Claude Code harness as a library (rung 3).
- [Mastra](https://mastra.ai/): a TypeScript agent framework with workflows, memory and tracing.
- [Cloudflare Agents](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/) and [Workers cron triggers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/cron-triggers/): the runtime and scheduling used in the walk-through.
- [tmux manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/tmux.1.html): `send-keys`, `capture-pane` and `-L` are enough to drive a lab.

### [Subagents and multi-agent work](../03-agents/03-subagents-and-multi-agent.md)

- [Claude Code CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference): `--resume`, `--fork-session` and the flags for scoping a worker's tools.
- [Codex CLI reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference): the equivalent commands in Codex, including `codex fork`.
- [git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree): the manual for the mechanism behind isolated workers.
- [A2A protocol](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A) and [samples](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-samples): the specification and runnable examples to explore with your agent.
- [Time-horizon measurements](https://metr.org/time-horizons/): how long a task current models can complete, useful when deciding what one agent can do alone.

### [Reliability, observability and evals](../03-agents/04-reliability-observability-evals.md)

- [Demystifying evals for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents): a thorough guide to case design, graders and eval-driven development.
- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/): open-source tracing and evals; its [Claude Code integration](https://langfuse.com/integrations/developer-tools/claude-code) lets you observe a coding harness.
- [Braintrust](https://www.braintrust.dev/): a hosted platform for traces, datasets and regression comparisons.
- [Promptfoo](https://www.promptfoo.dev/): an open-source eval runner with a CLI that fits in CI.
- [OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/): standard attribute names for model and tool spans.
- [Claude Code monitoring](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage): how to export a coding harness's usage, cost and tool activity.

## Part 4: Delivery with agents

### [Intent, specs and decomposition](../04-delivery/01-intent-specs-and-decomposition.md)

- [A public decisions folder](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/tree/main/docs/contributing/decisions): a real project with about a hundred short, agent-maintained records to learn the shape from.
- [Shape Up](https://basecamp.com/shapeup): shaping work, setting appetite and scoping before building. It predates agents and still applies.

### [The delivery loop](../04-delivery/02-the-delivery-loop.md)

- [Claude Code routines](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines): scheduled and event-triggered cloud runs. Check the page for current triggers and limits.
- [Claude Code on the web](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web): cloud sessions that do not depend on your machine.
- [Codex cloud](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud): the equivalent for Codex.
- [GitHub Actions documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions): the common place to run event-triggered checks and agents next to a repo.
- [A public "harness engineering" guide](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/blob/main/docs/contributing/harness-engineering.md): one project's written loop from intent to enforcement, worth reading as a worked example.

### [Verification and quality gates](../04-delivery/03-verification-and-quality-gates.md)

- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/): browser automation with video recording, screenshots and traces, usable from a script an agent writes.
- [A public validate workflow](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/blob/main/.github/workflows/validate.yml): a real CI gate with about thirty checks, from formatting to browser tests.
- [The custom check scripts behind it](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/tree/main/tools): house rules as code, including checks for docs and decision records. Good material to discuss with your own agent.
- [Skill: create a verification skill](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md): generates a project-local skill that starts your app, drives it the way a user does and captures evidence.
- [Skill: maintain a verification skill](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md): the periodic pass that keeps that skill and its feature notes in step with the app.
- [Knip](https://knip.dev/): finds unused files, exports and dependencies, a cheap deterministic gate against leftovers.
- [Browserbase](https://www.browserbase.com/): hosted browsers for agents when local machines cannot run enough of them.

### [PR review with agents](../04-delivery/04-pr-review-with-agents.md)

- [Git hooks documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks): `pre-push` and the other client-side hooks, for a guard that also covers a plain terminal.
- [About pull request reviews (GitHub Docs)](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews): review states, threads and required reviews.
- [Claude Code GitHub Actions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions): running an agent reviewer from CI or from a PR comment.
- [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/docs/bugbot) and [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai/): hosted agent reviewers, useful as a comparison for your own review skill.

### [Learning after release](../04-delivery/05-learning-after-release.md)

- [A public friction log guide](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/blob/main/docs/contributing/friction-log.md): the issue format and daily sweep described above, as one project runs them.
- [A decision record with a dated follow-up note](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/blob/main/docs/contributing/decisions/0056-cli-credential-bootstrap.md): what "the rule and why it changed" looks like after a friction report.
- [A public disaster recovery document](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/blob/main/docs/contributing/disaster-recovery.md): recovery steps with a live evidence log, kept current by agents.
- [Cleanup after migrations](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/blob/main/docs/contributing/cleanup-after-migrations.md): a written rule for removing the old path once the new one is live.
- [Sentry](https://sentry.io/): error tracking, with automated root-cause analysis that can be handed to a coding agent.
- [PostHog](https://posthog.com/): product events, funnels, session recordings and feature flags in one place.
- [OpenFeature](https://openfeature.dev/): a vendor-neutral API for feature flags, useful if you do not want to tie code to one provider.

## Part 5: Autonomy

### [Autonomous systems](../05-autonomy/01-autonomous-systems.md)

- [systemd](https://systemd.io/): user units and timers for starting, restarting and scheduling jobs on Linux.
- [Cloudflare Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/): one example of a stateful runtime with built-in alarms, useful as a model of durable execution.

### [Portable agent config](../05-autonomy/02-portable-agent-config.md)

- [Kody](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody): an open-source MCP server that carries memory, credentials and automations across harnesses; worth reading for its design.
- [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/): the protocol behind the gateway approach.
- [AgentFS](https://www.agentfs.ai/): a sandboxed, auditable filesystem for agents; in beta, useful as a source of ideas for isolation and rollback.

### [Orchestrating agent teams](../05-autonomy/03-orchestrating-agent-teams.md)

- [Limen](https://github.com/overment/limen): a minimal one-human-many-agents harness built from files, git and one CLI; read it for the job, note and review mechanics.
- [Herdr](https://herdr.dev/) and its [repository](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr): a workspace for running many agent sessions in panes, with a command line agents can drive.

### [Events, hooks and pipelines](../05-autonomy/04-events-hooks-and-pipelines.md)

- [GitHub webhooks documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks): event types and delivery behaviour, including redelivery, for mention and CI triggers.

### [Self-improving systems](../05-autonomy/05-self-improving-systems.md)

- [OpenAI evals guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evals): the same ground from another vendor; useful for grader design.

## Part 6: Field guides

### [An always-on remote setup: a blueprint](../06-field-guides/02-always-on-remote-setup-blueprint.md)

- [Claude Code: Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control): the vendor's documentation for channel 2, with current flags.
- [Tailscale Serve](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailscale-serve): how a localhost port is offered to the tailnet only.
- [tmux wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki): separate servers with `-L`, `capture-pane` and `send-keys`.
- [gh auth setup-git](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_setup-git): makes git use the GitHub CLI as its credential helper.

### [Working habits and anti-patterns](../06-field-guides/03-working-habits-and-anti-patterns.md)

- [Claude Code documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs): reference for `/compact`, hooks and subagents.
- [Claude Code checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing): what `/rewind` restores and what it does not track.
